key_insight: eMOOD replaces MOOD’s relaxed maximum-principle detector with an entropy-based troubled-cell indicator that flags non-smooth regions more selectively, enabling efficient shock capturing on unstructured meshes.
engineering_relevance: This makes high-order finite-volume solvers for compressible multiphase flows faster and more scalable by reducing unnecessary limiter activation, memory traffic, and reconstruction cost.
method: Uses numerical entropy production as a compact-stencil troubled-cell detector.
Integrates the detector into both classical MOOD cascades and a MOOD-CWENO hybrid.
Deploys in UCNS3D for unstructured-mesh, parallel shock-capturing simulations.
evidence_signal: Across Shu-Osher, double Mach reflection, forward-facing step, shock-helium-bubble, and triple-material-point benchmarks, the method reduced flagged cells by up to 75% and delivered speed-ups of up to 20% while preserving solution quality.
watch_item: Entropy-based detection must be tuned carefully for complex flows, since overly aggressive or overly conservative thresholds could misclassify weak gradients or under-resolved interfaces.
paper_title: eMOOD: Entropy-Based Multidimensional Optimal Order Detection for High-Order Shock-Capturing Finite-Volume Schemes
